annotations.text:
Butterloom — mobile-first, low fidelity.

390 × 844 phone frames. The dashed rule marks the fold on the screens that run past it.

Grey bars are copy nobody has written yet. [BRACKETS] are facts or decisions nobody has settled. Product names, prices and the TrxID are sample values.

Catalogue — cached at the edge, so it arrives in one round trip from Dhaka.

The 2 beside Cart is the only per-visitor pixel on the page: read from the client-readable cookie by part of the 1–2KB JS budget. With JS off the badge is just the word Cart.

Nothing here says whether the piece is in stock, and nothing should: a cached page that asserts nothing about stock cannot go stale into a lie (ADR-0007).

Add to cart is the first POST allowed to set a cookie, so it is an uncached path.

One shot above the buy block and the rest below it. The current markup stacks every photograph above the price, which on a phone pushes ৳6,400 a screen and a half down — worth a decision.

Uncached and cookie-keyed, so this page may carry per-visitor truth without the caching rules biting.

The − and + are real submit buttons that POST and redirect; quantity needs no JS.

Delivery is priced by our own flat rule — Pathao is never asked for a live quote (ADR-0004).

One page, one POST. The selects work: city → zone → area, the cascade ADR-0004 makes mandatory, each step standing in for a fetch of one edge-cacheable option fragment rather than shipping the whole location tree.

The bKash reveal below it is CSS :has(), not script, so it costs nothing from the budget.

JS on this screen: the cascade and the cart badge. Nothing else.

The same screen with JavaScript off — the hard requirement, drawn rather than assumed.

Each Load button is a real submit; the page comes back with the next list filled in and the earlier answers kept. Two extra round trips from Dhaka, where the enhanced path costs none.

The cart badge is gone, because the count comes from the JS that is not running.

Option B, kept so the choice is on the table — not the recommendation.

For: three short screens read better on a phone, a mistake is cheaper to recover, and the JS-off path stops being a second path.

Against: two or three extra round trips from Dhaka on every checkout, which is the cost ADR-0007 spends the whole architecture avoiding, and a form that can be abandoned in three places instead of one.
